children.label: a
children.prompt: State why $\triangle LMP$ is similar to $\triangle PMN$.

answer.worked: Both triangles are right-angled at M. Since the outer triangle LPN is right-angled at P, its acute angles at L and N sum to $90^\circ$. The acute angles at P and N of triangle PMN also sum to $90^\circ$, so $\angle MLP=\angle MPN$. Therefore $\triangle LMP\sim\triangle PMN$ by AAA.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If $PM=10\text{ cm}$ and $MN=6\text{ cm}$, calculate LM.

answer.worked: Corresponding sides in $\triangle LMP\sim\triangle PMN$ give $\frac{LM}{PM}=\frac{PM}{MN}$. Thus $\frac{LM}{10}=\frac{10}{6}$, so $LM=\frac{100}{6}=\frac{50}{3}\text{ cm}$.
